title: Mohr–Pardey–Rautenbach conjecture on almost colour-balanced spanning forests
statement:
Let $K_n$ be the complete graph on $n$ vertices, and let $c:E(K_n)\rightarrow\{-1,+1\}$ be a **balanced colouring**, meaning that $c(K_n)=0$. Let $F$ be an $n$-vertex forest with maximum degree $\Delta$.

**Mohr–Pardey–Rautenbach conjecture.** There exists a copy $F'$ of $F$ in $K_n$ such that

$$
\left|c(F')\right|\leq \tfrac{1}{2}(\Delta-1).
$$

This conjecture asks how close to colour-balanced a spanning copy of an arbitrary forest can be in a balanced two-colouring of the complete graph. It generalises known results for perfect matchings, factors of paths, and spanning paths; its general case is presented as open in the source.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.06148

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2024).
source_name: Lawrence Hollom, Adva Mond and Julien Portier, “Almost colour-balanced spanning forests in complete graphs”, arXiv:2410.06148 (2024).
